Level 1 · Introduction · Week 2

Loop-de-Loop

Loops repeat steps so we don't have to.

What you will learn

  • How repeat and forever loops save you from copying blocks.
  • How to make a sprite walk by switching costumes.
  • How to draw with the Pen and make shapes with the rule turn = 360 ÷ sides.

The big idea

Look at these two scripts. They draw the same square! The left one copies the same two blocks four times. The right one uses a loop.

=

  • repeat 4 runs the blocks inside it 4 times, then the program carries on.

  • forever runs the blocks inside it again and again until you click the red stop sign.

How much to turn?

When you walk all the way around a shape, you turn all the way around once. A whole turn is 360 degrees. So each corner turn is:

turn = 360 ÷ number of sides

The arrows show the turn at each corner. Big arrows = big turns.

Fill in the table. (Tip: you can let Scratch divide! Put the green “( ) / ( )” block from Operators into the turn slot.)

Shape Sides Repeat Turn (degrees)
Triangle 3 3 120
Square 4 (blank to fill in) (blank to fill in)
Pentagon 5
Hexagon 6
Octagon 8

Exercise2.1: Walking Cat

Make the cat walk back and forth forever.

  1. Start a new project (File → New). Click the Costumes tab: the cat has 2 costumes. Flipping between them looks like walking! Click Code to go back.

  2. Build this script. “set rotation style” keeps the cat from walking upside down.

  3. Click the flag. Click the red stop sign to stop.

Try it: what happens if you take out the “wait” block?

Exercise2.2: Polygon Party

Draw shapes with the Pen.

  1. Click the blue Add Extension button (bottom left) and choose Pen.

  2. Make the cat small: in the sprite pane, set Size to 40.

  3. Build the square script. Click the flag. Does the square close?

  4. Now change the numbers to draw a triangle, a hexagon and a pentagon. Use your table!

Bug hunt! Leo wanted a triangle. He used
repeat 3, move 100, turn 60.
Predict: what will it draw?

Run it. What is the bug, and what is the fix?

New words

loop
Code that repeats.
repeat
A loop that runs a set number of times, then stops.
forever
A loop that keeps going until you click stop.
costume
One picture of a sprite. Switching costumes makes animation.
extension
Extra blocks you add to Scratch, like the Pen.
degrees
How we measure turns. A whole turn is 360 degrees.

Homework: Loop-de-Loop

15–20 minutes. Do Core first; Challenge and Creative are optional.

CoreShape Gallery (Scratch, about 10 minutes)

Draw a triangle, a square and a hexagon in a row, like pictures in a gallery.

  1. Open Scratch. Click Add Extension (bottom left) and choose Pen. Set the cat’s Size to 40.

  2. Build the script. “pen up” before each “go to” stops the cat drawing a line between the shapes.

  3. Fill in the two missing numbers for the hexagon (use the rule turn = 360 ÷ sides).

  4. Click the flag. Save as shape-gallery.

(The right-hand stack snaps under the left-hand one: it is one long script, split in two to fit the page.)

My hexagon numbers: repeat (blank to fill in) turn (blank to fill in)
